summary: Caldas stands under the national framework of Colombia. The source inventory for this department contains no Caldas-specific findings on law, enforcement, documents, entry screening, facilities, care access or violence, so the national assessment carried by the parent record applies without local qualification.
tangentialFactors: The national baseline against which Caldas is assessed includes documented transfemicide and organised threat campaigns in other Colombian departments. El País reported 13 trans people killed in Colombia in the first quarter of 2025, and The Guardian recorded 41 trans women killed in 2023 with a further eight between February and April 2024. Armed groups in Caquetá circulated 'social cleansing' flyers and gave trans woman Tatiana Cespedes one week to leave town or be killed; an activist quoted in that investigation stated the prosecutor's office does not recognise transfemicide and records such killings as ordinary cases. None of these incidents occurred in Caldas, and neither report contains Caldas-specific information.
localsOnly: No resident-facing facts specific to Caldas were identified in the source inventory. The department's residents stand under Colombia's national legal gender recognition regime, notary-based marker changes and Constitutional Court protections as carried by the parent record.
outOfScopeNotes: Whether Caldas has experienced armed-group 'social cleansing' flyer campaigns, transfemicide incidents, or departmental protection-programme activity is unresolved: the inventory contains no reporting on Caldas in these areas. Local enforcement practice by Caldas notaries, prosecutors and police regarding trans people is likewise not sourced here.
